business_problem: Frankly.AI needed a faster way to turn AI-mediated interviews, panel transcripts and research papers into trustworthy summaries and queryable insights for public-sector consultation work.
solution_summary: Frankly.AI worked with IBM Customer Success and Client Engineering to build a proof-of-concept on IBM watsonx.ai and IBM Watson Discovery for the New Zealand AI Forum consultation workflow. The system ingests forum discussion transcripts plus associated research papers, then uses Smart Document Understanding in Watson Discovery to organize the material by topic, speaker and other relevant parameters. On top of that indexed corpus, watsonx.ai runs each user query through pre-trained large language models to return concise, targeted insights inside the consultation chatbot. Rather than simply collect opinions, the implementation turns multi-source discussion content into a searchable evidence base that can be used to draft a white paper and surface the most relevant perspectives across a broad community of stakeholders.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Runs pre-trained large language models to answer user questions with concise, targeted insights.

solution_components.name: IBM Watson Discovery
solution_components.role: Organizes transcripts and research papers by topic, speaker and related parameters using Smart Document Understanding.

data_flow: Forum discussion transcripts and associated research papers are ingested into Watson Discovery, organized with Smart Document Understanding, and then passed to watsonx.ai so the consultation chatbot can answer user-specific questions and support white-paper creation.
business_outcome: The two-week proof of concept cut reporting time by more than 90% and enabled roughly 100 New Zealand AI Forum members to generate a white paper from the proceedings faster and with more targeted insight.
metrics: roughly 100 members of the New Zealand AI Forum used the POC solution
